stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one

Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Treat observed object cells as shape evidence, not proof of how they relate to the rest of the grid: enumerate plausible roles (template, marker, or output component) and test each against the full grid and demos before committing. For apparently noisy backgrounds, test candidate patterns against the background values and distinguish exact matches from approximate/noisy matches rather than inferring a target or transformation from resemblance alone.
3. Infer output dimensions and the value of every cell, not only the changed ones. When a uniform full row or column separates panels, test whether the output is one panel or combines information across panels; dimensions alone do not establish which. For a demonstrated rule that recolors cells strictly between same-color markers on a shared row or column, test consecutive marker pairs in each row and column; preserve markers and all cells outside those segments. Finally validate row count, row lengths, values (0–9), and JSON before submitting.
4. After feedback, revise the hypothesis only from the correctness result or a new demo. A correct/incorrect result does not identify which cells were wrong; do not treat speculative explanations as evidence. Submit only when the rule is sufficiently supported; use `finish` only after the instance is over.
